paragraphs.source_en: When I first settled in this house, no one welcomed me except the master. Wherever I went, they shoved me away, and not a single person would have anything to do with me. How little I was valued may be seen well enough from the fact that even to this day they have not given me a name. Having no other choice, I did my best to stay near the master who had taken me in. Every morning, when the master read the newspaper, I would invariably sit on his knees. When he took his afternoon nap, I would lie on his back. This was not because I was especially fond of the master, but simply because no one else would bother with me. Later, as I gained experience, I took to lying on the rice tub in the morning, on the kotatsu at night, and out on the veranda at noon when the weather was fine. But what I found most comfortable was to slip into the children’s bedding at night and sleep together with them. The two little girls in this house, one five and the other three, slept alone together in one room every night, sharing the same bedding. I would always find a space between them and contrive somehow to squeeze myself in. But if my luck was bad and one of the children woke up, disaster would be upon me. The children, especially the younger one, who had the worse temper, would cry out loudly in the middle of the night: “The cat’s here! The cat’s here!” Then the master with the nervous stomach trouble would inevitably wake up and come rushing in from the next room. Why, only the other day he beat me soundly on the backside with a ruler.

paragraphs.source_zh: 我在这个家里住下来的当初，除了主人外，我不受任何人的欢迎。不管走到哪里，他们都对我推推搡搡，没有一个人搭理我。我如此不受重视，只要从直到今天还不给我起名字一事，就不难看出吧。我万般无奈，只好尽量呆在收留我的主人身旁。每天清晨，主人读报的时候，我总是坐在他的膝头上。他睡午觉时，我就趴在他的脊背上。这倒不是说我喜欢主人，而是因为没有人搭理我而不得已如此罢了。后来我的经验丰富了，每天清晨就趴在盛热饭的小木桶上，晚上睡在“被炉”上，天气晴朗的晌午，就躺在走廊里。我感到最舒服的还是夜里钻进孩子们的被窝，同他们一起睡觉。这家的两个小女孩，一个五岁，一个三岁，每天夜里两个孩子单独睡在一间屋，并且同睡一个被窝。我总是在她们中间找出个容身之地，想方设法挤进去。可是，有时运气不佳，一旦有个孩子醒来，我就大祸临头了。两个孩子——尤其那个岁数小的脾气最坏——会不顾深更半夜大声哭喊：“猫来了！猫来了！”于是，那个有神经性胃痛的主人必定醒来，从邻室跑过来。就拿前几天来说吧，他用尺子在我的屁股上狠打了一通。

paragraphs.source_en: Living with human beings and observing them closely, I have come to declare that they are all exceedingly selfish. The two little girls with whom I often share the bedclothes are especially outrageous. When the fancy takes them, they do whatever they please: hold me upside down, put a paper bag over my head, throw me out, or stuff me into the stove. Yet if I so much as try to strike back, the whole household mobilizes, chases me everywhere, and persecutes me. The other day, when I merely sharpened my claws a little on the matting, the mistress flew into a rage. Since then I have hardly been allowed into the sitting room. Even if I shiver all over on the kitchen floor, they remain utterly unconcerned. The white cat across the way, whom I greatly respect, tells me whenever we meet, “There is nothing more heartless than human beings.” A few days ago, the white cat gave birth to four beautiful, jewel-like kittens, but on the third day the student in her household took them to the pond behind the house and threw every one of them in. With hot tears, the white cat told me the whole story from beginning to end, then said, “If we cats are to fulfill the love between parent and child and enjoy a happy family life, we must wage war on human beings and utterly exterminate them!” I found her argument reasonable in every particular. The tortoiseshell next door, too, once said to me with great indignation, “Human beings have no understanding whatever of ownership.” According to the usual custom among us cats, whether it is the head of a dried sardine or the innards of a mullet, whoever finds it first has the right to eat it. If the other party fails to observe this rule, one may resort to force. But human beings clearly have not the slightest notion of this, for delicacies we have found are invariably seized by them. Relying always on their superior strength, they coolly snatch away what should rightfully be ours to eat. The white cat lives in a soldier’s house; the tortoiseshell’s master is a lawyer. Because I live in a teacher’s house, I am rather more optimistic about such matters than those two. I am quite content if I can somehow get through each day as it comes. Human beings though they are, surely they cannot prosper forever. Let us wait patiently for the coming of the age when cats shall have their day.

units.source_en: Living with human beings and observing them closely, I have come to declare that they are all exceedingly selfish.
units.source_zh: 我和人同居，经过仔细观察，我断言他们都是极其任性的。

units.source_en: The two little girls with whom I often share the bedclothes are especially outrageous.
units.source_zh: 尤其是两个经常和我同衾的小女孩，更是无法无天。

units.source_en: When the fancy takes them, they do whatever they please: hold me upside down, put a paper bag over my head, throw me out, or stuff me into the stove.
units.source_zh: 她们一时高兴，便任意胡来，把我倒拎着，或者往我头上套纸袋，要不就把我扔出去，或者塞进炉灶里面。

units.source_en: Yet if I so much as try to strike back, the whole household mobilizes, chases me everywhere, and persecutes me.
units.source_zh: 可是，我只要稍一还手，他们就会全家总动员，四处追我，对我加以迫害。

units.source_en: The other day, when I merely sharpened my claws a little on the matting, the mistress flew into a rage.
units.source_zh: 前几天，我在席子上稍微磨了一下爪子，女主人立刻大发雷霆。

units.source_en: Since then I have hardly been allowed into the sitting room.
units.source_zh: 从那以后，轻易不允许我进入客厅。

units.source_en: Even if I shiver all over on the kitchen floor, they remain utterly unconcerned.
units.source_zh: 我即使在厨房的地板上冻得浑身打战，他们也无动于衷。

units.source_en: The white cat across the way, whom I greatly respect, tells me whenever we meet, “There is nothing more heartless than human beings.”
units.source_zh: 令我敬佩的、住在对街的白娘子，每次和我见面，总是告诉我：“再也没有比人类更冷酷无情的啦。”

units.source_en: A few days ago, the white cat gave birth to four beautiful, jewel-like kittens, but on the third day the student in her household took them to the pond behind the house and threw every one of them in.

ja.t: まれたのである。ところがそこの

units.source_zh: 前些天，白娘子生下四只俊俏可爱的小猫，可是谁知她家的书生第三天就把他们弄到后院，一只不剩地扔进了水池子里。

units.source_en: With hot tears, the white cat told me the whole story from beginning to end, then said, “If we cats are to fulfill the love between parent and child and enjoy a happy family life, we must wage war on human beings and utterly exterminate them!”

ja.t: せねばならぬ」といわれた。

units.source_zh: 白娘子流着热泪原原本本向我诉说了这件事儿，然后说：“为了实现我们猫族的母子之爱，为了我们能过上美满的家庭生活，我们必须向人类开战，非将他们除尽杀绝不可！”

units.source_en: I found her argument reasonable in every particular.
units.source_zh: 我觉得她的见解入情入理。

units.source_en: The tortoiseshell next door, too, once said to me with great indignation, “Human beings have no understanding whatever of ownership.”
units.source_zh: 还有隔壁的三毛君，也非常愤慨地对我说：“人类根本不懂得什么叫所有权。”

units.source_en: According to the usual custom among us cats, whether it is the head of a dried sardine or the innards of a mullet, whoever finds it first has the right to eat it.

ja.t: があるものとなっている。

units.source_zh: 按我们猫族的常规来说，不管是沙丁鱼串的鱼头，还是鲻鱼的肠子，谁先找到，谁就有吃的权利。

units.source_en: If the other party fails to observe this rule, one may resort to force.
units.source_zh: 如果对方不遵守这个规矩，便可以诉诸武力。

units.source_en: But human beings clearly have not the slightest notion of this, for delicacies we have found are invariably seized by them.
units.source_zh: 但是人类显然丝毫没有这种观念，我们找到了美味佳肴，他们必然会夺去。

units.source_en: Relying always on their superior strength, they coolly snatch away what should rightfully be ours to eat.
units.source_zh: 他们总是依仗自己力气大，若无其事地抢走理应归我们吃的东西。

units.source_en: The white cat lives in a soldier’s house;
units.source_zh: 白娘子住在军人家里；

units.source_en: the tortoiseshell’s master is a lawyer.
units.source_zh: 三毛君的主人是个律师。

units.source_en: Because I live in a teacher’s house, I am rather more optimistic about such matters than those two.
units.source_zh: 我因为住在教师家里，对待这类事儿比起他们两位来要乐观得多。

units.source_en: I am quite content if I can somehow get through each day as it comes.
units.source_zh: 我只要能够一天一天地对付下去就心满意足了。

units.source_en: Human beings though they are, surely they cannot prosper forever.

ja.t: だって、そういつまでも

units.source_zh: 别看他们是人类，也未必永远繁荣昌盛吧。

units.source_en: Let us wait patiently for the coming of the age when cats shall have their day.
units.source_zh: 让我们耐心等待“猫儿走运的时代”到来吧！

paragraphs.source_zh: 我和人同居，经过仔细观察，我断言他们都是极其任性的。尤其是两个经常和我同衾的小女孩，更是无法无天。她们一时高兴，便任意胡来，把我倒拎着，或者往我头上套纸袋，要不就把我扔出去，或者塞进炉灶里面。可是，我只要稍一还手，他们就会全家总动员，四处追我，对我加以迫害。前几天，我在席子上稍微磨了一下爪子，女主人立刻大发雷霆。从那以后，轻易不允许我进入客厅。我即使在厨房的地板上冻得浑身打战，他们也无动于衷。令我敬佩的、住在对街的白娘子，每次和我见面，总是告诉我：“再也没有比人类更冷酷无情的啦。”前些天，白娘子生下四只俊俏可爱的小猫，可是谁知她家的书生第三天就把他们弄到后院，一只不剩地扔进了水池子里。白娘子流着热泪原原本本向我诉说了这件事儿，然后说：“为了实现我们猫族的母子之爱，为了我们能过上美满的家庭生活，我们必须向人类开战，非将他们除尽杀绝不可！”我觉得她的见解入情入理。还有隔壁的三毛君，也非常愤慨地对我说：“人类根本不懂得什么叫所有权。”按我们猫族的常规来说，不管是沙丁鱼串的鱼头，还是鲻鱼的肠子，谁先找到，谁就有吃的权利。如果对方不遵守这个规矩，便可以诉诸武力。但是人类显然丝毫没有这种观念，我们找到了美味佳肴，他们必然会夺去。他们总是依仗自己力气大，若无其事地抢走理应归我们吃的东西。白娘子住在军人家里；三毛君的主人是个律师。我因为住在教师家里，对待这类事儿比起他们两位来要乐观得多。我只要能够一天一天地对付下去就心满意足了。别看他们是人类，也未必永远繁荣昌盛吧。让我们耐心等待“猫儿走运的时代”到来吧！
